hypothesis: The Icarus Verilog 12 -g2012 compile still aborts because the physical register file in rtl/prf.sv uses an aggregate/whole-array reset assignment such as `prf_regs <= '0;` inside an always_ff block. Icarus reports 'Assignment to an entire array or to an array slice is not yet supported' for that construct and the subsequent packed_dimensions assertion during elaboration is triggered while elaborating the same unsupported array assignment. Previous repairs focused on cache/BTB arrays but did not inspect prf.sv, where a register-file reset almost always uses the prohibited whole-array write. The fix must replace the aggregate reset with an explicit per-entry reset (e.g. a generate loop or hand-unrolled always_ff per physical register) while preserving the module ports and the write/read behavior.
constraints: Do not change the prf module port names, widths, or directions.
Reset must clear every physical register without using whole-array or array-slice assignment; use explicit per-entry reset logic.
Write port updates only the selected register index when prf_write_valid is high, and read ports must remain combinational.
Keep the physical register count and indexing scheme unchanged.
verification_targets: Icarus Verilog 12 -g2012 compilation exits successfully with no 'Assignment to an entire array or to an array slice is not yet supported' errors and no elab_expr assertion.
After reset deassertion, all physical registers read back 0.
A write to a physical register followed by a read to the same index returns the written data in the same simulation.
